newsitem.title: UK: Taxman thwarts any Burmah special dividends.
newsitem.headline: Taxman thwarts any Burmah special dividends.

text.p: Burmah Castrol said it was studying the possibility of a special dividend to reach a more optimal capital structure, but added it had no current plans for any extra pay-outs as these would be heavily taxed.
"We do look at it as a possibility, but currently we don't have a plan for a special dividend because of the tax penalty," Burmah's finance director Brian Hardy told a news conference.

A special dividend would reduce the company's average cost of capital, which might also be achieved by borrowing more money. With a gearing of 28 percent, Burmah said it could borrow a lot extra without endangering its financial strength.

"Theorists would tell you that our debt should be something like 300 million stg," said Fry. By contrast, Burmah's net borrowings will stand somewhere near 100 million by the end of this year, he added.
But while Burmah could easily find banks willing to lend it money, it would have the problem of not knowing how to spend it, chief executive Jonathan Fry said.

Burmah could make a big acquisition in the chemicals industry, but it is not inclinded to do that after it was criticised in the early 1990s for making a purchase just at the beginning of an economic downturn.
Burmah is still busy appeasing financial markets.

"Our chemical policy has not been fully accepted yet," said Fry, explaining why a big chemicals deal was not on the cards now. To change the market attitude Burmah will meet analysts in November, he added.
"We have to convince them and then the mood might change. But at the moment they don't trust us," Fry said after the news conference.
He added that Burmah would love to expand more rapidly in fast-growing Asian lubricants markets, but the problem there was people rather than money.
"There is a human limit there," Fry said, adding it was hard to find people with sufficient language skills.
"And once you've found somebody, they are pinched," he added.
